title: PLACEBO-ENTRY: does the ARENA-13 protocol inflate whoever enters through it, and is the +0.045 residue real at all? (arm A zero calls; arm B 1,192 calls)
question: Arm A: refit the twelve on their answer-disagreeing subset; arm B: re-enter gemini (already on the board, original traces, no REGEN) through the ARENA-13 protocol: 4 opponents x 150, disagreement-filtered, leave-out ensemble reference, dual order; both boards centred on the other eleven; registered: gemini's theta gains >= +0.045 with a CI excluding zero.

registration.heading: ## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any call) — PLACEBO-ENTRY: does the ARENA-13 PROTOCOL inflate whoever enters through it?
outcome_heading: L1734: - **PLACEBO-ENTRY OUTCOME (2026-09-14): the hypothesis is NOT CONFIRMED, the free precursor that supported it

review.file: the ledger audit (same hour, 2026-09-14): the first version compared the protocol's four-opponent theta against gemini's ELEVEN-opponent x12 theta and read +0.013; matched, the sign flips to -0.043
review.verdict: NOT CONFIRMED (delta -0.043 [-0.196, +0.109], under-powered); QUESTION DISSOLVED by the free check (4): the residue's CI includes zero; methodological rule adopted

criteria.text: gemini's theta gains >= +0.045 with a CI excluding zero
criteria.value: arm B delta -0.043 [-0.196, +0.109] against the MATCHED four-opponent baseline; POWER: CI half-width 0.152 against a +0.045 bar, so this arm could not have confirmed the hypothesis even if true: NOT CONFIRMED is absence of evidence; the amendment rule that would have blamed trace style is WITHDRAWN, not applied

criteria.text: refit the twelve on the answer-disagreeing subset
criteria.value: filtering widens the theta scale 13% (SD 1.785 vs 1.574) and moves top models +0.17..+0.37 from the centre: looked supportive; reconciled with arm B because arm A refits EVERY model on filtered evidence (a global rescaling) while arm B changes ONE model's edges against four

criteria.text: free check: the newcomer's dual-order theta gap to gemini
criteria.value: +0.045 with a bootstrap CI of [-0.068, +0.186]: includes zero; there is no residue to explain; quality-not-in-the-key and trace style are withdrawn as questions

falsifier.note: METHODOLOGICAL RULE ADOPTED: every rank-based pass/fail criterion needs a resolution check (a CI on the quantity that sets the rank) before a FAIL can be read as mis-ranking; applies retrospectively to ARENA-V2-X20's top-6 clause and to any future LADDER-INSERT; the second cheap proxy that day to overstate an effect after POSITION-DECOMP's 7x imputation error

sentence_of_record: PLACEBO-ENTRY (2026-09-14, 1,192 calls): arm A looked supportive (filtering widens the theta scale 13%); arm B NOT CONFIRMED, delta -0.043 [-0.196, +0.109] against the matched four-opponent baseline (CORRECTION, ledger audit, same hour: the first version compared against gemini's eleven-opponent x12 theta and read +0.013; the sign flips once matched); power: CI half-width 0.152 against a +0.045 bar, so NOT CONFIRMED is absence of evidence and the amendment rule is WITHDRAWN, not applied; (4) the free check that settles the line: the newcomer's dual-order theta gap to gemini is +0.045 with CI [-0.068, +0.186], it includes zero, there is no residue to explain. METHODOLOGICAL RULE ADOPTED: every rank-based pass/fail criterion needs a resolution check before a FAIL can be read as mis-ranking.

plain_description.what: Asks whether the protocol for adding a new model to the arena inflates the newcomer's score, and whether a small +0.045 advantage seen earlier is real. One arm uses existing data, the other 1,192 judge calls.
plain_description.why: It checks that the leaderboard is fair to models that join later.
plain_description.information: Inflation would mean the entry protocol biases rankings. Result: not confirmed, but the test was under-powered, so this is absence of evidence. The +0.045 gap's interval includes zero, so there is no residue to explain. It led to a rule: any rank-based pass/fail needs a resolution check first. A later ruling classes this run's judged data as history.
